title: What to do when the weather turns

sections.h: A shortlist for a rainy day
p: Beach days get rained out here more than anyone likes. The good news is that the indoor options are broad. WonderWorks, Ripley's Aquarium, Ripley's Believe It or Not! and the Hollywood Wax Museum are the large attractions, most of them close together around Broadway at the Beach and the oceanfront. EdVenture is a children's museum built for younger kids, and the Myrtle Beach Pinball Museum lets you play the machines.

For active groups, trampoline parks like Sky Zone and Big Air burn off energy. Bowling at the 810 Billiards and Bowling locations, Stars and Strikes or AlleyOops works for mixed ages, and Dave and Buster's covers the arcade crowd. Jack Axe Throwing and Pin Point Indoor Pickleball and Golf are good for teens and adults.

There are a lot of escape rooms here, which is useful when you want to compare themes. Escapology, The Escape Game, Riddles, Captive Escape Rooms, Backstage Escape Games, Myrtle Beach Room Escape and Break Out Myrtle Beach all take small groups through timed puzzle rooms. Most last about an hour. Some require an adult for younger guests, so check age rules when you book.

Two spots in this list have you make something. Black Flag Forge in Myrtle Beach is a blacksmithing workshop, and Conway Glass in Conway is a glass studio. They are small and book by appointment, so they work as a half-day plan for older kids and adults. Ripley's Haunted Adventure and the mirror mazes are quicker.

list: Rainy days fill indoor places fast. Book timed tickets and escape rooms early in the day or the day before.
Group the big attractions by location so you are not driving between North Myrtle Beach and Myrtle Beach in the rain.
Look for combo tickets if you plan on more than one of the big attractions, and check each attraction's own page for current prices.
